summary: This is an e-commerce executive dashboard called Orbit Ops, displaying key business metrics (Revenue, Orders, Refund Rate), a weekly sales bar chart, and recent customer order records.

stack.name: Next.js (App Router)
stack.why: Provides React SSR/SSG and integrated server actions/API routes for streamlined full-stack development.

stack.name: Tailwind CSS
stack.why: Enables rapid styling with customizable design tokens matching the provided color palette.

stack.name: Recharts
stack.why: Lightweight, customizable SVG charting library ideal for rendering the weekly sales bar chart.

stack.name: PostgreSQL via Supabase
stack.why: Provides hosted relational storage and ready-to-use row-level security and authentication.

stack.name: Vercel
stack.why: First-class deployment platform for Next.js applications with zero-config setup.

steps.title: Initialize project and install dependencies
steps.detail: Create a new Next.js project with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS configured, then install lucide-react and recharts.
steps.code:
npx create-next-app@latest orbit-ops --typescript --tailwind --app
cd orbit-ops && npm install recharts lucide-react
steps.check: Development server starts with `npm run dev` and loads the starter page.

steps.check: Background color `bg-page` compiles correctly and styles the canvas.

behaviour: Typing in 'Search orders...' filters the table rows by customer name or order number in real-time.
Clicking sidebar menu items updates the active navigation state and routes to corresponding pages.
Hovering over weekly sales bars reveals tooltip showing exact sales quantity or revenue for that period.
Clicking an order row navigates to an order detail modal or drawer (likely).
data: Aggregated metrics: total revenue amount, count of orders, refund percentage
Weekly sales series: day/week buckets and corresponding sales figures
Recent orders list: order ID number, customer full name, order status (Shipped, Pending, Refunded), and dollar total

backend.summary: Express or Next.js server exposing REST endpoints to calculate dashboard aggregates and return paginated order lists.
backend.database: PostgreSQL because relational schemas reliably handle order transactions and aggregate reporting.
backend.auth: JWT-based session authentication via HTTP-only cookies managed through Supabase Auth.

tables.name: orders
tables.columns: id uuid pk, order_number int unique, customer_id uuid, status varchar(20), total numeric(10,2), created_at timestamp

tables.name: customers
tables.columns: id uuid pk, name varchar(100), email varchar(100) unique, created_at timestamp

endpoints.purpose: Calculates and returns total revenue, order count, and refund rate over current period.
Returns daily aggregated sales values for the 7-day bar chart.
Fetches recent orders with optional search query filter.

rules: Total order amounts must be non-negative numbers.
Refund rate is calculated as (count of refunded orders / total orders) * 100.

pitfalls: Hardcoding chart container height incorrectly, causing Recharts ResponsiveContainer to collapse to 0px height.
Not handling empty search states or case-insensitive matching when querying customer names.
Failing to fix sidebar width, causing the main layout to jitter on smaller desktop viewports.
testing: Verify StatCard renders formatted currency '$48,210' and refund rate '2.1%'.
Test that filtering by 'Leo' reduces table to 1 row containing order #10420.
Assert that 7 bars are rendered inside the WeeklySalesChart SVG element.
deploy: Import repository into Vercel and set up environment variables for Supabase database access.
Run Supabase migration scripts to initialize Postgres schema and seed data.

tokens.method: Colours: pixel quantisation of the whole screenshot and of each detected element. Font sizes: text box height ÷ 1.25. Spacing: gaps between sibling boxes, snapped to a 4px grid. Measured approximations, not values read from source code.
